events.name: TECHNOVA 2026 Championship Overview
events.description: TECHNOVA 2026 is the Inter-House Robotics & Artificial Intelligence Championship hosted by City Montessori School, Aliganj-I. Dates: 19 and 20 November 2026. Principal: Ms. Shivani Singh. Participants: Classes VI-XII, subject to category eligibility. Format: Inter-House team and individual challenges. Reporting time: 8:00 AM on the respective event day. Host branch: CMS Aliganj-I.

events.name: TECHNOVA Registration
events.description: Registration form: https://forms.gle/YT72wa7RzUM5qmGM7. The registration deadline was 16 November 2026. This published deadline has passed. The brochure does not confirm late registration. Contact the event organisers to ask whether any exception is possible.

events.name: Robo Soccer
events.description: Junior Section, Classes VI-VIII. Date: 20 November 2026. Objective: score goals using a remotely controlled robot. Team: maximum 2 members, one robot. Maximum robot dimensions: 30 x 30 x 30 cm; maximum weight: 3 kg. Wired or wireless remote; autonomous functions permitted but not required. Maximum power: 12V. Robots must not hold or trap the ball. Match: two halves of 2 minutes with a 1-minute half-time. Fouls include holding or trapping the ball for more than 5 seconds and deliberate damaging contact. Penalty: free kick to the non-offending team, with the opponent robot 30 cm away from the ball. Winner: most goals. Venue: Turf Area, Cambridge Section. Teacher: Mr. Shantanu Kumar. Disqualification: non-compliant robot, deliberate damage to opponent robot or field, more than 3 foul warnings in a match, or unsportsmanlike conduct.

events.name: Line Follower
events.description: Junior Section, Classes VI-VIII. Date: 20 November 2026. Objective: a fully autonomous robot follows a black line on a white surface and completes the track in the shortest time. Remote control is not allowed after the run begins. Sensors: 3 individual IR sensors. Maximum dimensions: 20 x 20 x 20 cm at the start. Maximum weight: 2 kg. Self-contained onboard power source, maximum 12V. Track: black line approximately 2-3 cm wide, with straight paths, curves and intersections. Start and finish boxes: solid black, 25 x 25 cm. Team: 2 participants. Two attempts with a 1-minute gap; the better time counts. Venue: Robotics Lab. Teacher: Ms. Noopur Goel. Disqualification: failure to meet specifications, human intervention after crossing the start line, or damage to the track or arena.

events.name: Obstacle Race
events.description: Date: 20 November 2026. Objective: navigate an obstacle arena and reach the finish in the shortest time. Control: wireless remote or Bluetooth. Maximum dimensions: 25 x 25 x 25 cm. Maximum weight: 3 kg. Onboard power: maximum 12V. Possible obstacles include ramps, bridges, speed breakers, sand, stones and pebbles. Team: 2 participants. One attempt, maximum 10 minutes. Up to 3 re-entries are allowed; the robot is placed at the last crossed checkpoint and the timer continues. Venue: Back Field. Teacher: Mr. Shubham Asthana. Disqualification: non-compliant robot or touching the robot after the start signal without judges' approval.

events.name: Robo War Balloon Bust
events.description: Date: 20 November 2026. Controlled robot-versus-robot challenge. Team: maximum 2 members. Maximum dimensions: 30 x 30 x 30 cm. Maximum weight: 5 kg including batteries. Control: remote or Bluetooth. Maximum power: 12V. Wedges, scoops or hoists are permitted subject to safety inspection. Destructive or offensive weapons and systems designed to dismantle an opponent robot are prohibited. Mandatory pre-event safety inspection applies. Sharp edges, projectiles, flames, hazardous substances and mechanisms likely to injure participants or spectators are prohibited. Barriers, emergency shutdown and judge intervention will be briefed before the event. Venue: Turf Area, Cambridge Section. Teacher: Ms. Swaranjali Rawat.

events.name: Boat Race
events.description: Senior Section only, Classes IX-XII. Date: 20 November 2026. Teams of 2 design and operate a self-propelled model boat demonstrating stability, propulsion and safe water operation. Battery electric motors. Maximum length: 30 cm. Maximum width: 20 cm. Lightweight, waterproof and environmentally responsible materials are encouraged. Boats undergo stability and electrical safety inspection. Venue: Swimming Pool, CMS Aliganj-I. Teacher: Mr. Shobhit Kanchan. Bring the completed boat and permitted onboard power source for inspection. No exposed or unsafe electrical connections. Follow marshal instructions for placing, operating and retrieving boats. Do not enter the water or retrieve a boat without authorisation. Race distance, heats, lane allocation and winner selection will be announced at the briefing.

events.name: AI Model Development Challenge
events.description: AI & Computing Arena. Team: 2 participants. Duration: 1 hour. Participants train a simple image, sound or gesture classifier using a beginner-friendly tool and test it on unseen examples. Focus areas: data labelling, training, testing and model limitations. The arena heading identifies Senior Section, Classes IX-XI, while the detailed table lists Classes IX-XII. Confirm eligibility with organisers. The brochure does not specify this challenge in the final event schedule, so its date and slot are unconfirmed.

events.name: Computer Vision Challenge
events.description: Date: 20 November 2026. AI & Computing Arena. Team: 2 participants. Duration: 1 hour. Use a prepared image set and starter code, such as OpenCV or a pre-trained model, to detect, count or classify shapes, colours or traffic signs. Focus areas: image preprocessing, detection, accuracy and limitations caused by lighting or blur. Eligibility discrepancy: arena heading says Classes IX-XI, detailed table says Classes IX-XII. Confirm with organisers. Venue: AI Lab. Teacher: To be announced.

events.name: NLP Challenge
events.description: Date: 20 November 2026. AI & Computing Arena. Team: 2 participants. Duration: 1 hour. Participants work with prepared short texts, clean and tokenise them, and build a sentiment or topic classifier in Python. Focus areas: text preprocessing, features, evaluation and bias in language data. Eligibility discrepancy: arena heading says Classes IX-XI, detailed table says Classes IX-XII. Confirm with organisers. Venue: AI Lab. Teacher: To be announced.

events.name: Game Development
events.description: Date: 20 November 2026. AI & Computing Arena. Team: 2 participants. Duration: 1 hour. Design and build a simple playable computer game on the approved platform. Judging considers logic, functionality, creativity and ability to explain the code. Eligibility discrepancy: arena heading says Classes IX-XI, detailed table says Classes IX-XII. Confirm with organisers. Venue: AI Lab. Teacher: Mr. Shubham Asthana.

events.name: AI and Robotics Quiz Challenge
events.description: Date: 19 November 2026. Duration: 1 hour. Rounds cover robotics fundamentals, AI concepts, sensors, programming logic, applications and responsible AI. Round structure and scoring will be explained before the quiz. The detailed table lists Classes IX-XII, while the arena heading says Classes IX-XI. Confirm eligibility with organisers. Venue: Computer / AI Lab. Teacher: Ms. Manju Rawat. Reporting time: 8:00 AM; slot to be announced. Team size is not specified in the brochure.

events.name: Mini Python Chatbot
events.description: AI & Computing Arena. Team: 2 participants. Duration: 1 hour. Build a rule-based school helpdesk or library chatbot using strings, dictionaries, conditional statements and functions. The detailed table lists Classes IX-XII, while the arena heading says Classes IX-XI. Confirm eligibility with organisers. This challenge is not included in the final schedule on page 8; its date, venue and slot are unconfirmed.

events.name: AI Innovation Showdown
events.description: Senior Section, Classes IX-XI. Date: 20 November 2026. Venue: AI Lab. Propose or demonstrate an AI-enabled solution to a meaningful real-world problem, preferably aligned with a Sustainable Development Goal. Entries may be prototypes, simulations or evidence-supported concepts. A working demonstration is encouraged. Presentation: 8 minutes total, maximum 5 minutes presentation and 3 minutes Q&A. Include problem statement, solution overview, AI and technical approach, impact and evidence, limitations and responsibility (bias, privacy, reliability and accessibility), and future scope. Judging out of 60 marks: problem relevance and clarity 10; technical understanding and use of AI 15; prototype/demo/feasibility 15; data/evidence/testing 10; originality/potential impact 5; communication/Q&A 5. Teacher: Mr. Abhishek Sharma.

events.name: TECHNOVA Rules and General Arrangements
events.description: Every team must register under the correct class group and category before the deadline. Participants must reach the designated venue at the communicated reporting time. Bring only equipment permitted by category rules; robots and boats are subject to technical inspection. For AI challenges, the host provides computers and pre-installed software wherever applicable. Internet, generative AI assistants, external storage devices and pre-written code are governed by category-specific instructions. Students must explain their own code, calculations, data and design decisions. Judges' decisions on scoring, safety and rule interpretation are final, subject to the announced procedure. Respect others and take care of the arena, equipment and other teams' property.
